sentences.text: Garudimimus was an ornithomimosaur that possessed a mix of ancestral and advanced anatomical traits.
Its skull was small relative to its body and completely lacked teeth in both the upper and lower jaws.
This relatively small dinosaur measured nearly 3.5 meters in length and weighed between 77.3 and 98 kilograms.
The axis vertebra was short, measuring about 3 cm in length and 1.8 cm in height, likely representing a primitive trait for ornithomimosaurs.
Unfused vertebrae suggest the holotype specimen was a still-growing sub-adult animal.
The known specimen of Garudimimus measured nearly 3.5 meters in length and weighed between 77.3 and 98 kilograms.
The genus Garudimimus was formally described by Rinchen Barsbold in 1981.
The only known specimen was found in 1981 by a Soviet-Mongolian expedition at Bayshin Tsav in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Southeastern Mongolia.
The lower edges of the premaxilla bone were thin and sharply developed.
Garudimimus was an omnivore or herbivore with a reduced bite force compensated by a horny beak.
The front parts of Garudimimus's upper and lower jaws were covered by a beak that likely helped it pluck food.
Cuff and Rayfield tentatively concluded that Garudimimus used its low bite force and beak to hold plant material while its neck muscles plucked vegetation.
Researchers Cuff and Rayfield suggested that the low bite force measured in Garudimimus might be due to the use of a different species' jaw in reconstructions or because the specimen was a sub-adult.
An analysis of scleral rings indicated that Garudimimus was a cathemeral herbivore.
The pelvic girdle and hindlimbs of Garudimimus indicate poor cursorial running capacities.
Garudimimus was one of the earliest ornithomimosaurians and does not seem to have been as well adapted for speed as more derived ornithomimids.
Garudimimus likely had shaggy feathering similar to large paleognath birds like ratites.
Garudimimus and Deinocheirus possess unique jaw muscle attachment sites featuring a triangular adductor complex attached to an expanding surangular bone.
Nabavizadeh described ornithomimosaurs, including Garudimimus, as orthal feeders that raised their jaws isognathously so that upper and lower teeth on each side contacted simultaneously.
Button and Zanno noted that there is no consistent relationship between herbivory and body size in ornithomimosaurs, as larger size does not always correlate with herbivory in this group.
Button and Zanno concluded that similar feeding strategies evolved independently in unrelated herbivorous dinosaur lineages over time.
The only known species of Garudimimus is Garudimimus brevipes.
In 1981, Barsbold classified Garudimimus in its own family, Garudimimidae, due to unusual morphological features.
Garudimimus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in Asia.
Garudimimus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 98 to 90 million years ago, between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages, in what is now Asia.
Garudimimus fossils were found in the Late Cretaceous Bayan Shireh Formation at the Bayshin Tsav locality.
Some researchers claimed Garudimimus possessed a nasal horn similar to that of Pelecanimimus.
It is debated whether large holes and deep depressions on the front neural arches indicate that the tail bones were air-spaced.
